ranked_facts.why: The flat rod electroretinogram is more characteristic of Retinitis Pigmentosa and Enhanced S-cone Syndrome than Congenital Stationary Night Blindness, but the presence of night blindness since childhood and other clinical features make Goldman-Favre Syndrome less likely.

The complete loss of photoreceptors, ellipsoid zone, and retinal pigment epithelium in the superotemporal region is more consistent with the progressive degeneration seen in Retinitis Pigmentosa than the stationary nature of Congenital Stationary Night Blindness or the characteristic findings in Enhanced S-cone Syndrome and Goldman-Favre Syndrome.
